 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the Act'), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 11.10.2010.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 11.10.2010 at about 7:30 p.m., he was proceeding from Gulbarga city bus stand to Kalbennur village in KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-32-F-0932 ('offending vehicle' for short).
Due to rash or negligent driving of the said bus, when the driver suddenly applied break, petitioner fell down on the ground and sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite prolonged treatment, petitioner is not completely cured.
As the owner and internal insurer, respondent is liable to pay the compensation.

4. Respondent has filed written statement disputing that the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment and prays to dismiss the appeal.
5. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

6. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 7.
7.
On behalf of respondent, R.W.1 is examined, however, no documents are marked.

8. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.1,03,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent to pay the same as detailed below:
Sl. Nature of the heads Compensation No.
1. Loss of future income Rs.73,440/-
2. Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/-
3. Loss of income during Rs.4,500/-

2 treatment 4.

Medical expenses Rs.5,000/-
5. Food, nutrition and Rs.10,000/-
 attendant charges  during treatment

Total Rs.1,02,940/-
 (rounded off) Rs.1,03,000/-
9.
Respondent has not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
10. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the compensation granted under all the heads is also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
11. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

12. Heard arguments and perused the records.
13.

Having regard to the fact that the respondent has not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the petitioner sustained injuries has attained finality.

14. As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 27 years and therefore,
multiplier 17 taken by the Tribunal is correct.

In the absence of proof of exact income,
the Tribunal has taken his notional income at Rs.4,500/- p.m.
Since the accident is of the year 2010, based on minimum wages, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.5,500/- p.m.
Based on the record, the Tribunal has rightly considered the disability at 8%.

With these components, the loss of income due to disability is at Rs.5,500/- x 12 x 17 x 8% =
89,760/- as against Rs.73,440/- granted by the Tribunal.
15. Based on medical bills, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.5,000/- under the head medical expenses is correct.
At the rate of Rs.5,500/- for a period of three months petitioner is entitled compensation in a sum of Rs.16,500/- under the head laid up period as against Rs.4,500/- granted by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the period of treatment and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability, the compensation granted in a sum of Rs.10,000/- each under the head pain & suffering and food nutrition and attendant charges is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/- and 20,000/- respectively.
The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head loss of amenities of life.

The same is quantified at Rs.25,000/-.
17.

Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.1,86,260/- together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.1,03,000/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount awarded Amount awarded by No. by the Tribunal this Court 1. Loss of future Rs.73,440/- Rs.89,760/-
income 2. Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/- Rs.30,000/-

3 . Loss of income Rs.4,500/- Rs.16,500/-
during treatment 4. Medical expenses Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,000/-

5. Food, nutrition and Rs.10,000/- Rs.20,000/-
attendant charges during treatment 6. Loss of amenities ----- Rs.25,000/-
Of course as the internal insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent is liable to pay the enhanced compensation with accrued interest.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.1,86,260/- together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.1,03,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
